unlisted_practices: Curtail the use of large language models in medical decision making until improved iterations undergo rigorous clinical validation.
Do not use LLMs to seek clinical advice outside the user's own medical expertise.
Do not dispatch consultative LLMs in lieu of infectious diseases clinicians.
Include education on AI in infectious diseases training programs and continuing medical education.

Involve infectious diseases clinicians in the development and oversight of LLM products, including identifying suitable problems, developing training and evaluation datasets, and designing prospective clinical trials.
Do not enter protected patient information into publicly available LLMs that may harvest user input for further training.
Validate LLM chatbots extensively and exercise caution before deploying them for patient-facing emotional support or queries.
Do not use black box models for high-stakes decisions; use interpretable models instead.
Advocate through regulatory agencies and professional societies for safe, patient-centered development of LLM technology.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary/narrative review discussing the limitations, risks, and necessary governance/engagement by clinicians regarding large language models in infectious disease consultation.
